newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BAN ON SAMPDORIA PLAYER HALVED AFTER PROTESTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAN ON SAMPDORIA PLAYER HALVED AFTER PROTESTS.

text.p: The Italian soccer federation has halved a controversial four-match ban on Sampdoria defender Sinisa Mihajlovic after a referee had a change of heart, an official said on Saturday.

Yugoslavia's Mihajlovic was given the severe ban earlier this month following a Sunday league match, when he kicked the ball in the direction of the referee and insulted him after a penalty had been awarded to opponents Atalanta.

Sampdoria's general director Emiliano Salvarezza called the ban "shameful and squalid" and the club's fans held a minute's silence at the start of last Sunday's league encounter to protest against the punishment.

The federation's disciplinary committee reduced the ban to two games after the match referee Salvatore Racalbuto changed his report to say that Mihajlovic had kicked the ball "towards" him "in a non-violent fashion" and not "against" him, as he had previously written.
Mihajlovic will have to sit out this weekend's match against Piacenza but will be back for Sampdoria's subsequent league game against Parma.
